notes:
## Page content

The sheet continues with a four-row list (70) of prospaces and index conditions. It describes V_J^L as a finite direct limit of those prospaces with semi-simplicial morphisms. A revised following sentence selects a system stable under intersections, gives the longer-index family (71), and describes maps using inclusions of flags satisfying the stated endpoint conditions. Formula (72) introduces the corresponding ordered flag set. The last paragraph describes a covering and writes the cohomological expression (73) for a sheaf F.

The oblique NB note singles out the case J intersection L equals the empty set. The written sign is phi-shaped, and the note ends with the separately underlined words quatre and cas. Several intervening words are still uncertain; their text and insertion order have not been reconstructed from the mathematical context.

## Mathematics-triggered rereadings

The set condition in the note prompted inspection of the complete glyph: it has an oval and an extended axial shaft, so phi is preserved as the written form. Its empty-set meaning is explained here rather than used to substitute a different glyph.

Both limit signs were inspected independently. The first main-paragraph lim has a clear right-facing triangular arrowhead beneath it. The replacement above cancelled recollement has a long bar ending in a short downward terminal; it does not expose a distinct arrowhead. The latter therefore remains varinjlim versus underlined lim, without transferring the first sign’s certainty to it.

The possible change of struck les Vijk into a live phrase in H prompted review of the entire revision. Those words remain on the cancelled opening baseline. The separate stable par intersections is singular and attaches after de proespaces. No intersection argument was used to manufacture the wording.

All of (72), not only its C mark, was reread. The two inclusions, both occurrences of I, the L and J of the first Drap, and union L in the middle argument are visible. The rewritten J and adjacent doubled brace-like stroke remain a combined doubt, including its deletion state. No balanced-brace correction has been imposed.

The raised pair after drapeaux has a continuous dash, not dots. Its curved leader explains the apparent comma and apparent strike through qui: neither is an independent mark. Qui and sont are live. The opening quotation is two high ticks and there is no closing quotation or full stop.

Both ends of the arrow after d in (73) were inspected. The left end has no bar, so the written arrow is a plain right arrow. The larger left-pointing double-shaft arrow, the index 2 on E, p and q, X primes and closing curves at the sheet edge were also read.

These are transcription checks of ink and placement, not proof verification. No mathematical proof or computational check was performed; check_events is empty.

## Cancellations, doubts and possible slips

All fourteen C deletion/insertion items are reviewed separately. In particular, the cancelled last word after qui en could be C’s résultent or H’s explicite; the crossing strokes do not permit certainty. The cancelled les/Vijk, recollement and avec les flèches de retain their doubts. The four unresolved supplied marginal marks are narrowed where individual words are legible. The comma after the marginal (70) remains uncertain.

There is no explicit author question mark, date or title on this sheet. The crossed and rewritten passages are author revisions, not proof corrections supplied by this reading. No mathematical slip is silently repaired. The unclosed opening quotation and the uncertain brace-like remnant are preserved.

## Sheet, numbering and line count

This is a handwritten text sheet, with four braced/equational displays and no genuine diagram or drawing. C’s diagram wrapper around (70) describes an ordinary four-row display and has been replaced by plain display syntax without a collation row. The source underlining in NB, quatre, cas, satisfaisant and conditions précédentes is retained.

The dark upper-left 38 is the author’s page number. The thin grey lower-left 83 belongs to a later foliation hand and is transcribed as a marginal number; H omits it. Scan 84 is archive metadata, not another handwritten number.

Line_count is 40: 29 main-column physical writing baselines, counting the four rows of (70), its raised addition, main prose, the separately cancelled lines, the other raised additions, three rows of (71), and the one-line displays (72)/(73); nine baselines in the slanted note including its two-line insertion; and two isolated numbering baselines. Formula labels that share a display’s baseline are not counted again. This is a count of writing baselines, not TeX source lines.

Abbreviation stops were inspected separately: ens has no terminal stop, while p.ex has a stop after p and none after x before the comma. No expansion is inserted into the text.

### Blind reading corrections

The live phrase after un système reads des proespaces: a third low s follows de. Formula (71) has a dot and rule in its V subscript, a dot and rule between inequalities, and two dots in the membership list, with no second comma in that list. The crossed line above les flèches is best read as uncertain au lieu de. The opening quotation ticks lie on the raised index insertion, immediately before its opening parenthesis; their former attachment before drapeaux is corrected. In (73), the small inner closing parenthesis is visible and a separate lower fragment of the outer closing curve reaches the clipped right edge, so the outer character is now explicitly uncertain. The marginal note remains locally uncertain as before; the blind alternatives did not establish clearer replacements for its retouched words.
